items.translatedQuestion: How was the Danxia landform in Shaoguan formed?
items.translatedAnswer: Geological studies show that 25 million years ago this area was a low-lying lake. Later, movements of the Earth's crust raised the land and the lake drained away, forming towering peaks. The sediments on the lakebed oxidized and turned into red rock.

items.translatedQuestion: Who named this red sandstone landform the Danxia landform?
items.translatedAnswer: In the 1930s, Chen Guoda, a professor at Sun Yat-sen University, conducted in-depth studies of Danxia Mountain and the red-rock mountains of South China and named this type of red sandstone terrain the Danxia landform. The name was soon accepted and adopted by the academic community. Since then, landforms around the world formed of red conglomerate and characterized by sheer red cliffs have been called Danxia landforms.

items.translatedQuestion: Why are the peaks along the Jinjiang River called “A Herd of Elephants Crossing the River”?
items.translatedAnswer: The peaks look like a herd of elephants about to cross the Jinjiang River and come toward us. Their trunks, tusks, ears, and eyes are all vividly recognizable, so the scene is called “A Herd of Elephants Crossing the River.”

items.translatedQuestion: Why is the distant mountain to your right, as viewed from Yangyuan Bridge, called “Jade Maiden Blocking the River”?
items.translatedAnswer: Look at the mountain in the distance to your right. It resembles a sleeping young woman; from right to left, you can make out her head, neck, chest, and abdomen, with a clearly defined outline. That is why the scene is called “Sleeping Beauty” or “Jade Maiden Blocking the River.”

items.translatedQuestion: Please tell us about Yangyuan Mountain at Shaoguan's Danxia Mountain.
items.translatedAnswer: This is Yangyuan Mountain, or “the male mountain.” This pillar of rock, called Yangyuan Stone, is 28 meters high and 7 meters in diameter and closely resembles a phallus; it is the reason for the mountain's name. Experts believe that Yangyuan Stone was originally part of the mountain's cliff face, from which the forces of nature separated and sculpted it into its present shape over 300,000 years ago. In the past, people prayed for male descendants to flourish and for their family line to continue, so the stone was often worshipped.

items.translatedQuestion: What honors and titles have been bestowed on the Kaiping Diaolou?
items.translatedAnswer: The Kaiping Diaolou are acclaimed as “a model of overseas Chinese culture” and “a museum of world architectural art.” They have been designated a National Key Cultural Relic Protection Site by the State Council. At their peak, there were 3,300 towers; today, 1,833 are officially registered. The site has been designated a National Key Cultural Relic Protection Site by the State Council, and 20 of the better-preserved towers have been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

items.translatedQuestion: What are the three main types of Kaiping Diaolou?
items.translatedAnswer: These buildings fall into three types: residential towers for individual families; communal towers built with contributions from villagers; and watchtowers, used mainly to keep watch and guard against bandits.

items.translatedQuestion: Please describe the structure and decoration of the diaolou in Zili Village.
items.translatedAnswer: The most exquisitely decorated tower is Mingshi Tower, a reinforced-concrete residence built in 1925. It is five stories high. At the center of the roof is a hexagonal lookout pavilion combining Chinese and Western styles, and each corner of the fifth floor has a corner turret, also known as a “swallow's nest.” The tower is large and imposing, with a heavy iron door and sturdy iron windows. Its interior is sumptuously furnished and has complete living facilities.

items.translatedQuestion: Why did Xie Weili, a Chinese American, name his garden Li Garden?
items.translatedAnswer: The garden's name, Li, comes from its owner's name and expresses the meaning of the Chinese idiom xiushen liben (修身立本), which is inscribed on an archway in the garden. It means that self-cultivation is the foundation for conducting oneself and establishing a family. The owner's philosophy is also reflected in many other inscriptions and couplets in the garden.

items.translatedQuestion: Why do we say that the residential buildings in Li Garden combine Chinese and Western architectural elements?
items.translatedAnswer: The villa roofs follow the style of Chinese palatial architecture, while the building exteriors are Western in style. The staircases, floors, and wall decorations inside also combine Chinese and Western elements, including Western fireplaces and chandeliers, Italian tiles, Chinese rosewood furniture, murals depicting folk tales, and gilded woodcarvings.

items.translatedQuestion: Why did Sun Yat-sen give up hope in the Qing government and decide to overthrow it?
items.translatedAnswer: China's defeats at the hands of foreign invaders, together with the Qing government's corruption and incompetence, intensified his patriotic indignation. He concluded that the Qing court was rotten to the core and had to be overthrown and replaced by a democratic republic.

items.translatedQuestion: When and where did Sun Yat-sen establish China's first political party?
items.translatedAnswer: In 1905, Sun Yat-sen went to Japan and founded China's first political party there, the Chinese Revolutionary Alliance (Tongmenghui). It later developed into the Kuomintang.

items.translatedQuestion: Please briefly introduce the designer of Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall.
items.translatedAnswer: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall was designed by Lu Yanzhi, an outstanding architect in modern China. Born in Tianjin, Lu graduated from Tsinghua University in Beijing and later went to Cornell University in the United States to study architecture. He died of lung cancer in 1929, before the memorial hall was completed, at just 36 years of age.

items.translatedQuestion: What are the distinctive features of Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall's appearance and construction?
items.translatedAnswer: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall is an octagonal, palace-style reinforced-concrete building. Its exterior follows the style of traditional Chinese architecture, while its structure employed the most advanced building technology of the time. The main building is 58 meters high and has a floor area of 12,000 square meters.

items.translatedQuestion: What modern architectural techniques did the designer use to build Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall?
items.translatedAnswer: Thanks to the designer's ingenious plan, the auditorium has excellent acoustics and the audience's view is unobstructed by columns. The eight massive columns supporting the four large-span steel trusses—which carry the huge domed roof—are cleverly concealed inside the walls.

items.translatedQuestion: Please introduce the occupant of the Nanyue King Tomb.
items.translatedAnswer: The tomb's occupant, Zhao Mo, was the second king of Nanyue. He succeeded to the throne in the fourth year of Emperor Wu of Han's Jianyuan era, took the title Emperor Wen, and reigned for 16 years (137–122 BCE).

items.translatedQuestion: Where did archaeologists excavate the remains of the Nanyue Kingdom palace?
items.translatedAnswer: Archaeologists carried out a trial excavation east of the former Children's Park in Guangzhou and uncovered about 500 square meters of the Nanyue Kingdom palace site.

items.translatedQuestion: Which gold seal was the first imperial seal unearthed through archaeological excavation in China?
items.translatedAnswer: The gold seal inscribed “Wendi Xingxi” unearthed from the Nanyue King Tomb is the only surviving seal of a Qin or Han emperor to have been recovered in an archaeological excavation in China.

items.translatedQuestion: What does the inscribed bronze dagger-axe unearthed from the Nanyue King Tomb tell us about its background?
items.translatedAnswer: Among the weapons unearthed from the Nanyue King Tomb, one bronze dagger-axe bears the inscription “Chancellor Zhang Yi, fourth year of the King” (王四年相邦张义). This indicates that it was made under Zhang Yi's supervision during the reign of King Hui of Qin and brought from Qin to Nanyue.

items.translatedQuestion: How many people were buried as sacrificial victims in the Nanyue King Tomb? Who was in the front chamber, and who was in the outer coffin chamber?
items.translatedAnswer: A total of 15 people buried as sacrificial victims were found in the tomb. One was in the front chamber and held the title Jingxiangling (景巷令); another was in the outer coffin chamber and may have been a charioteer.

items.translatedQuestion: What functions did Chen Clan Ancestral Hall serve?
items.translatedAnswer: The Chen Clan Ancestral Hall was used to worship the clan's common ancestor and as a venue for clan activities on festive occasions and at other times. Also known as Chen Clan Academy, it served as a school where young members of the Chen clan studied.

items.translatedQuestion: Why is Chen Clan Ancestral Hall acclaimed as the “Pearl of Lingnan Architectural Art”?
items.translatedAnswer: In its architectural ornamentation, Chen Clan Ancestral Hall brings together the finest of Guangdong's folk crafts and is acclaimed as the “Pearl of Lingnan Architectural Art.” It was therefore converted into the Guangdong Folk Arts Museum in 1959.

items.translatedQuestion: Please describe the stone drums on either side of the main entrance to Chen Clan Ancestral Hall.
items.translatedAnswer: The stone drums on either side of the main entrance symbolize the family's status. In old feudal China, a family could place large drums in front of its residence only if one of its members had achieved the rank of jinshi or higher in the imperial examinations.

items.translatedQuestion: Please explain the “fortune has arrived” image at Chen Clan Ancestral Hall (the “fortune” character on the reverse side).
items.translatedAnswer: This is also the Chinese character for “fortune,” shown reversed from left to right. In Chinese, the word for “inverted” (倒, dào) is a homophone of the word for “arrived” (到, dào), so an inverted fortune character represents “fortune has arrived.”

items.translatedQuestion: Please explain the Lingnan fruit offerings at Chen Clan Ancestral Hall.
items.translatedAnswer: Various prized fruits from Lingnan are carved at the tops of the balusters on the platform, including peaches, star fruit, papaya, and lychees. These are symbolic offerings that members of the Chen clan presented to their ancestors.
